title: Interaction Costing Scratchpad
content:
Context / problem statement:
- Prod teams frequently ask: how much will a change (longer context, higher temperature, different model) actually cost in $/month?
- Console currently shows token usage and project-level spend, but there is no lightweight interactive estimator for planned changes.
- Sales / AE requests: quick per-route preview to show customers cost/performance tradeoffs during demos.

Goal (high level):
- Build a small interactive widget in Console + an internal CLI tool that can estimate per-interaction cost and latency implications for a given workload profile.
- Make the estimator actionable: show knobs (sequence length, batching, quantization profile, model variant, cache hit-rate) and estimated % change in monthly bill and tail latency.

Scope (MVP):
- Console widget on model-route page: "Interaction Estimator" panel with fields: avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, requests/day, target model variant, cache-hit fraction, batching window ms, target qos (p95 latency).
- Simple backend estimator service (stateless) that uses: per-model token-price map, historical throughput/latency profiles (from telemetry), and batching model to compute expected token/sec and queueing penalty.
- Export: CSV of scenario inputs and delta to current baseline.
- Internal CLI: same model but invoked locally for quick ad-hoc checks (supporting local config file).

Non-goals (MVP):
- Not full cost optimization engine or auto-suggested rollout policies (advanced follow-ups).
- No chargeable billing estimate (exact invoice) — only approximations for planning.

Assumptions / data needs:
- Need per-model effective unit token cost (hosted + infra overhead) — product finance to provide baseline rates (JIRA-INF-4821 assigned).
- Telemetry: token distribution, request size distribution, batching latency curves per model and GPU class from Observability team.
- Cache hit-rate: user-provided or inferred from prefix reuse heuristics.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I want to input a proposed average prompt length and projected daily requests so I can estimate monthly incremental spend for a new feature.
- As an SRE, I want to see p95 latency impact when turning on batching at different window sizes to understand tail amplification.
- As an AE, I want an exportable CSV in a demo to show a customer their projected bill change when moving from standard to dedciated capacity.

Key UX ideas / fields:
- Baseline selector: pick an existing route (pre-populate with telemetry) or blank scenario.
- Knobs: avg prompt tokens, avg reply tokens, requests/day, model, model-variant (quantized vs fp16), batching window (ms), cache-hit %, reserved capacity (dedicated pool vs hosted), region selector.
- Visuals: mini-sankey for token flow (in/out + cache saved), delta bar showing % increase/decrease vs baseline, small latency vs throughput curve preview.
- Quick-presets: "chat short", "longform summarization", "embedding bulk" presets.

Estimation model (sketch):
- cost_estimate = (tokens_in + tokens_out) * unit_cost_per_token * requests
- unit_cost_per_token = base_model_cost * model_factor * variant_factor * infra_factor
- latency_estimate = base_latency(model, seq_len) + batching_penalty(batching_window, qps) + queuing_model(qps, capacity)
- caching reduces tokens_in by cache_hit_rate * avg_prefix_tokens saved
- Add a safety buffer (default +10%) to account for measurement uncertainty

Data sources and integrations:
- Telemetry: query per-route stats (avg tokens, p50/p95 latency, qps distribution) via /observability/route-metrics API (work with observability).
- Pricing: static feed from finance (S3 or internal config) mapping model -> token price and capacity multipliers.
- Capacity profiles: single-number throughput and p95 curves per GPU class from infra (we can approximate using linear interpolation).

Metrics / success criteria (MVP):
- Adoption: 20 distinct teams try the estimator within first 6 weeks (tracked via telemetry event: estimator.run).
- Accuracy: estimator within +/- 20% of actual spend on retrospective test runs for 3 sample routes.
- UX task success: 80% of trial users can produce a CSV export in <3 minutes during usability tests.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 0: Kickoff + align on data contracts with Observability and Finance.
- Week 1-2: Backend estimator prototype (python microservice) + simple unit tests.
- Week 2-3: Console UI mockups + internal usability with PMs and AE.
- Week 3-4: Connect telemetry, validate against 5 historical routes, adjust model factors.
- Week 5: Beta release to internal teams + collect feedback, iterate.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How to present uncertainty? slider for safety buffer vs single conservative estimate?
- For Dedicated vs Hosted, do we model reserved commitments and amortize them across routes? (finance needs input)
- Should the estimator recommend concrete actions (enable prefix cache, lower temperature)? MVP: no, just show impacts.

Risks / mitigations:
- Telemetry noise -> add smoothing and require minimum sample size before pre-populating fields.
- Users may treat estimate as invoice -> add strong label: "planning estimates only; not a bill" and link to billing docs.
- Complexity creep -> keep UI minimal and conservative for MVP.

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Sync with Finance for unit token cost table (owner: Sam Ortiz)
- [ ] Observability API contract: route-metrics query (owner: Leo Wong)
- [ ] Draft UI sketches in Figma (owner: UX: Priya Desai)
- [ ] Prototype backend estimator + tests (owner: eng: Nora Bennett)
- [ ] Add telemetry ping for estimator runs and exports (owner: eng-observability)

Notes to self / idea parking lot:
- Could add "what-if" scenarios: e.g., show impact of 10% traffic growth OR sudden fall in cache-hit rate.
- Consider bundle-level amortization for Dedicated (if infra wants us to show per-route share).
- Long-term: couple estimator to Optimize so we can auto-suggest batching and quantization changes and estimate ROI.
- Would be cool to surface compute/energy estimate for sustainability reports (maybe later).

Quick mock command-line usage (internal):
- ri-estimate --model gptx-13b --prompt-tokens 120 --reply-tokens 450 --rps 2 --cache-hit 0.2 --variant int4 --batch-ms 20
- output: monthly_tokens, est_cost_usd, p95_latency_ms, notes

Slack threads and references:
- #prod-pricing (pinned messages)
- slack: thread linking to JIRA-INF-4821 for finance inputs

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after initial syncs.
